sources.evidence_scope: 2024 paper explicitly says slaving fleets declined drastically after Hawkins defeat but illicit small-scale activities continued, no complete abandonment; warns SlaveVoyages pre1570 records include incorrect ship attribution and 17 entries all from 3 Hawkins voyages; do NOT treat no database voyage entry as proof none occurred 1570–72.

discrepancies.note: DIB Devereux estimates 200 defenders plus 300–400 refugees, DIB Norreys around 600 victims total. Alternative numbers are related estimates, not additive.
£80k Crown cost, £35k Essex personal cost, £10k Queen loan and £5k proposed yearly Crown rents are mutually different categories, NOT profit or double-counted.
1400t ore cargo was worthless and no enduring settlement; £1000 queen share investment not UK gold receipts.
1577–80 expedition captures wealth 1579, return/distribution and Queen's actual fiscal impact 1580 and later; no imaginary year-1579 realized Exchequer net returns.

discrepancies.type: 1570s West African trade and alleged slaving continuity
discrepancies.note: Previous ch9 research summary said no corroborated NEW 1570s English Guinea slave voyage. More accurate: Winter fleet of three sent Guinea 1570 and one returned direct; Winter again 1571/Spanish Caribbean reports, three Hawkins-owned ships left for West Africa autumn1572 probably slaving. Records prove departures/plans at varying certainty; do NOT claim captive counts, successful African kidnapping, exact landfalls, or a 1570s British colony. EHR says drastic decline not total stop.
